beliefs.practice: Read the MongoDB/Cosmos connection string from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI / MONGO_URI) and never hard-code credentials in source; load secrets from Azure Key Vault in production.
Use TLS for all connections to the database (set tls=true/ssl=true in the MongoClient connection string) and validate server certificates, never disable certificate verification in production.
Use a long-lived MongoClient with connection pooling (configure maxPoolSize appropriately for app concurrency) and reuse that client across requests instead of creating a new client per HTTP request.

Enable and handle retryable writes and implement exponential backoff, and specifically detect and handle HTTP 429 / rate-limiting responses from Cosmos DB (respect Retry-After header) when provisioning RU-based throughput.
Provision read/write throughput appropriate for embedding and vector-search workloads (use autoscale or increase RU/s when indexing large batches) and monitor RU consumption and throttling metrics.

Store embedding metadata alongside the vector: include embedding model name, embedding_version, vector_dim, and a timestamp so you can re-embed or migrate later and ensure consistent dimensions are enforced at insert time.

Keep embedding vectors as a fixed dtype (prefer float32) and a consistent length; if using cosine similarity, store a normalized version of the embedding (unit-length) to make cosine equivalent to dot-product.

When storing embeddings in BSON, use a deterministic binary representation (e.g., serialize float32 little-endian into BSON Binary subtype) and document the serialization format so clients and index creation use the same layout.

Create vector indexes server-side with explicit algorithm and parameters (e.g., algorithm=IVF, metric=cosine or l2, set nlist appropriate to dataset) and make index creation idempotent (check for existing index before creating).

Tune IVF parameters relative to dataset size: pick nlist (number of inverted lists) proportional to sqrt(N) and set search params (nprobe) to trade recall vs latency; document chosen defaults and allow configuration.

When doing semantic search: first run the vector ANN search to get a small candidate set (e.g., top 100), then run a metadata filter/score over those candidates to apply business filters and finally return the top-k (e.g., 10) with only necessary fields projected.
Avoid returning the full embedding in API responses — project only the fields needed for the UI (title, description, product_id, score) to reduce transfer size and leakage of model vectors.

Cache embeddings for input texts (and cache common query embeddings) to avoid re-calling external embedding service for repeated inputs; cache should be invalidated if embedding model/version changes.
Use a deterministic mock embedder in unit tests and CI (as the sample does) and keep that behaviour behind an abstracted embedder interface so production and tests can swap easily.

Limit document size to the service's supported maximum (avoid very large payloads); for Cosmos DB/Azure DocumentDB APIs verify the max item size for the chosen API (SQL vs MongoDB) and keep documents well under that limit, e.g., split large content into separate storage like Blob Storage.

Instrument index creation and long-running operations (index build, bulk ingest) with logging and health checks; run index creation asynchronously and avoid blocking API traffic during large index builds, or build indexes during maintenance windows.

Apply appropriate partitioning/sharding key consistent with query patterns (choose a partition key that avoids hot partitions), and for read-heavy vector search keep metadata used to filter inside the same logical partition when possible.

Protect your OpenAI (or other embedding provider) API key: read it from env or Key Vault, add rate limiting on requests, and guard against accidental logging of the key or full requests in production logs.

When creating vector indexes via the MongoDB-compatible API, use server-side commands or createIndexes (not client-side in-memory structures) and verify the index exists and is usable before accepting search traffic.

Monitor production with Application Insights / metrics: track request latency, embedding API errors, RU consumption, index build status, and 429 occurrences; set alerts for sustained throttling or high error rates.
